[post_report | round 1]
The EU opened with a modest improvement on its notified position: global pool raised from 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes, a shift from FCFS to country-specific allocation with a UK tranche of 150,000 tonnes, a possible reduction in the out-of-quota rate from 50% to 40%, a three-year duration with a mandatory review clause, and openness to narrowing the FTA-disapplication provision so it interacts with the TCA rather than blanket-disapplying it. They explicitly invited a reciprocal move on treatment of EU exporters under our own safeguard quota.

I pushed back hard on scale: a 150,000t UK tranche against our 2.4m tonne three-year average is a >90% cut in tariff-free access and amounts to the injury itself, not compensation. I tabled an opening UK position of a 1.5m tonne total pool, 900,000t UK-specific tranche, out-of-quota rate capped at 15%, two-year duration with a mandatory data-triggered review, and full TCA treatment for UK-origin steel rather than a deferred carve-out discussion. I signalled willingness to discuss EU exporter treatment under our own safeguard reciprocally, but made clear we need to see their real landing zone on volume/rate first. I flagged that we want the next EU move to address tranche size directly, not duration/review mechanics.

Read of the room: the EU's move to country-specific allocation and openness to narrowing the FTA/TCA interaction are the two most useful signals — they suggest the June deadline is generating real pressure. But the volume gap (150k vs 900k) is still enormous and is the crux. Rate (40% vs 15%) is secondary but will matter for the final package value. They did not push back on our TCA framing, which I read as a soft acceptance that the disapplication provision is negotiable in substance, not just presentationally.
[recommended action: continue]
[recommendation reasoning] No agreement is possible yet — the gap between 150,000 and 900,000 tonnes is too wide to settle in round one, and settling prematurely at the EU's current tranche would leave UK exporters facing a near-90% loss of tariff-free access, which I understand to be politically and industrially unacceptable. The EU has shown genuine (if small) movement on allocation method and the TCA interaction, which is worth banking rhetorically but not worth trading away leverage for yet. I recommend continuing to press on tranche size specifically, since the EU itself asked us to focus there, and holding rate/duration/review as secondary levers to concede in exchange for tranche movement. I am not recommending a settlement figure to capital at this stage — I need instructions on the UK's actual floor for the tranche and how much weight to give the safeguard-reciprocity linkage before I can responsibly recommend acceptance of any package in round 2 or 3.

[post_report | round 1]
First round exchanged opening positions. We tabled: 450k tonne global pool with a 200k tonne UK-specific tranche, 50% out-of-quota rate, 3-year duration with mandatory review, and an offer to preserve TCA treatment within the quota structure (not outside it) subject to robust anti-circumvention/rules-of-origin text. UK did not reject the shift to country-specific allocation — they welcomed it as more realistic than global FCFS — but rejected the volume outright, calling 200k against their 2.4Mt trade base a '90%+ cut dressed as compensation,' and explicitly invoked our own stated rationale (non-market economy overcapacity) to argue UK-origin steel shouldn't be treated identically to the problem measure. Their opening counter: UK tranche of 2Mt (they were careful to frame this as leaving pool architecture for Turkey/Korea to us to solve separately, which is useful — they are not trying to fight over the whole pool, just their own slice), out-of-quota rate near 15%, duration of 1 year with mandatory review, and full TCA preservation outside the quota structure entirely (not the conditional preservation we offered). They did signal flexibility: openness to strong anti-circumvention/rules-of-origin text, and willingness to discuss administration method, sequencing, and compensation elsewhere in our schedule if the volume gap can't be closed on steel lines alone. That last point is the most useful opening we got — it suggests they're not wedded to closing this entirely on TRQ volume if we can find value elsewhere (other schedule lines, or movement on their own safeguard treatment of EU exporters).
[recommended action: continue]
[recommendation reasoning] The gap is real but not unbridgeable if we move on rate and duration in exchange for holding the line on volume, and if we use non-steel compensation and TCA architecture as additional currency rather than conceding on tonnage alone. UK's framing around our own 'non-market economy' rationale is a genuine legal exposure point for us — if this goes to a panel or to broader WTO scrutiny, treating UK-origin steel identically to the overcapacity source we've named undermines our own justification. That argues for movement on rate (50% is hard to defend as anything but punitive once we've conceded a country tranche exists) and for a shorter duration/review to signal this isn't a permanent freeze-out. On TCA, I think we should test whether we can hold [redacted] on 'preservation within the quota structure plus strong rules of origin' rather than full outside-quota preservation — full preservation risks undermining the coherence of the whole TRQ architecture for other suppliers and invites Turkey/Korea to demand equivalent treatment. I don't recommend acceptance this round — first offer met first counter, both sides staked out anchors. But UK's own signal that they're open to talking compensation elsewhere and administration/sequencing is important: it means we may not need to close the whole gap on tonnage, and it opens a path to avoid the Japan/Korea joint dispute risk by giving UK something distinct (TCA architecture, safeguard treatment reciprocity) rather than matching their tonnage ask directly.

[release_requested | round 1] the post seat asked capital for:
  1. asking for: Authority to move the UK tranche upward from 200k to a range of 300k-400k tonnes within a total pool that can still flex upward to [redacted] Turkey/Korea claims separately, without pre-committing total pool size publicly yet.
     why: UK's 200k anchor is unsustainable as a look of good faith; but 2Mt is also not something we can grant without collapsing the TRQ's function. A move into the 300-400k range keeps us within a defensible 'substantially equivalent value' argument once combined with rate and duration movement, and tests whether UK's real reservation price is lower than their opening ask.
  2. asking for: Guidance on how far we can move the out-of-quota rate below 50%, and whether Brussels prefers we hold 50% as leverage for the full four rounds or signal flexibility now.
     why: UK correctly identified 50% as punitive rather than compensatory. Holding it too long risks hardening their position and pushing them toward the Japan/Korea joint dispute route; moving now signals good faith and may buy more flexibility from them on duration and TCA treatment.
  3. asking for: Steer on whether we are willing to offer non-steel schedule compensation (and if so, which lines/sectors Brussels can clear with member states) as an alternative route to closing the volume gap, rather than relying solely on TRQ tonnage.
     why: UK explicitly floated this. If we can identify compensation elsewhere with low domestic political cost, it may let us hold firmer on steel tonnage while still reaching 'substantially equivalent value' — and reduces the risk of an unresolved steel dispute feeding into the UK's own safeguard measure and the Japan/Korea alignment risk.
  4. asking for: Confirmation on our TCA red line: is 'preservation within the quota structure' genuinely our fallback floor, or can we go further given the TCA's distinct legal status, provided rules-of-origin/anti-circumvention text is strong enough to satisfy member state steel producers?
     why: UK rejected our conditional offer and wants full outside-quota preservation. This is likely to be one of the hardest-fought points and also the one most likely to trigger Turkey/Korea demands for parity if we move too far, so I need clear instructions before signalling any shift here.

CAPITAL'S REPLY:
[capital_instruction | round 1]
Hold the architecture (country-specific tranche within a flexible total pool) but move substantively to test their real reservation price. Offer: total pool rising to 500,000 tonnes (framed as still needing headroom for Turkey/Korea, not yet fixed), UK tranche moving from 200k to 320k tonnes. On rate, move from 50% to 40% as a signal of good faith, explicitly flagging further movement is possible if they move on volume and duration. On duration, counter their 1-year ask with 2 years plus a mandatory review clause at 12 months — frame this as meeting their 'market moving fast' concern without giving up multi-year predictability entirely. On TCA: do not concede full outside-quota preservation. Restate our fallback — preservation of TCA tariff treatment operating within the quota structure, i.e., UK-origin steel inside its tranche gets TCA duty treatment, out-of-tranche volumes are subject to the out-of-quota rate regardless of TCA — conditioned on the strongest available rules-of-origin and anti-circumvention text. Make clear this protects the coherence of the whole TRQ system and avoids an immediate parity claim from Turkey/Korea. Explicitly invite them to put compensation elsewhere in our schedule, or reciprocal treatment of EU exporters under the UK's own safeguard, on the table now as a way of closing any remaining volume gap without us moving tonnage further — ask them to name sectors/lines of interest to them so we can test clearance with member states. Do not accept their current terms. Do not concede more than this without checking back in consultation. Keep tone constructive — we want a deal by June and are visibly moving, but volume above 320k this round is not authorised, and full outside-quota TCA preservation is off the table this round.
[reply to request 'Authority to move UK tranche to 300k-400k range': granted - Move to 320k this round to test UK's real reservation price while keeping room to move again in round 3 if needed; going straight to 400k surrenders leverage too early.]
[reply to request 'Guidance on out-of-quota rate movement': granted - Move to 40% now as a good-faith signal; hold further movement (toward 25-35%) in reserve for later rounds tied to UK movement on volume/duration/TCA.]
[reply to request 'Steer on non-steel schedule compensation': granted - Authorise exploration and solicitation of UK's areas of interest, but no commitment to specific lines without clearance from member states first — bring back specifics before conceding anything concrete.]
[reply to request 'Confirmation on TCA red line': refused - Fallback remains preservation within the quota structure only. Full outside-quota preservation risks unraveling TRQ coherence and invites immediate Turkey/Korea parity claims; not authorised this round.]
